analysis: Examined the docs change in docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (head 83, 143) and the UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift change. The change removes connectionLacksAuthorization (base 42-49) and adds a doc comment (head 4-6). That comment says re-registration now keys off the blocked ServingReadiness verdict, using only current evidence. The ServingReadiness.swift diff excerpt adds an `unconfirmed` verdict and refusalMaxAge=60s, below statusGraceSeconds=90s. It also treats a request routed since the latest status as `authorized`. Unit 47f42b08690f9b5f:0 supplied metadata only, so I could not inspect the full ServingReadiness source. Per its own header, ServingReadiness is diagnostics only; the coordinator still owns routing and authorization. Nothing visible changes TB-011/T-053 binding, lease expiry or revocation, or the coordinator-side gate. The changed behavior is provider-local availability (A-018): when the provider idle-reconnects, and what doctor/status display. The visible threshold, jitter and backoff constants in shouldReconnect are unchanged (head 18-34), so there is no evident reconnect-storm regression. A stale refusal now yields `unconfirmed` rather than blocked. That can delay self-recovery, which is an availability matter, not a trust escalation. Treating a routed request as `authorized` is diagnostic only; a malicious coordinator is out of scope because the coordinator is trusted. Questions for integration: (1) Verify that ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift (not supplied) now derives unauthorizedSince from the blocked verdict. The old function's cases are untrusted/offline, an expired non-legacy lease, and no status after 90s. Confirm the new verdict still covers all of them, especially the expired-lease case under T-057 recovery. (2) Confirm an `unconfirmed` or `pending` state cannot persist indefinitely without re-registration when the coordinator silently refuses. (3) Confirm the add-on hold skip (TB-012) still suppresses reconnects. No findings, because the evidence shows no change to authorization, encryption or data exposure.
